en.title: Ignoring Complete 1-to-0 Intervals
en.description:
From left to right, delete each complete interval that starts with a 1 and ends at the first 0 after it, including both ends. Meeting another 1 inside an interval does not reset its start. A trailing segment with no closing 0 is kept in full, and all other elements are kept in their original order; also return the sum of the kept elements. The outputs of original examples 2 and 4 contradict the statement and explanation; this site corrects them according to the explicit statement.

The input and output format was prepared by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers. 1≤n≤100000, −10⁹≤element≤10⁹.
en.output: The first line is the number of kept elements m; the second line contains m integers (an empty line when m=0); the third line is the sum, which needs a 64-bit integer.
en.explanation: Example 1: delete 1, 7, 0 and keep 6, 2, 5, 6, 1, 3, sum 23. Example 2: neither of the two later 1s has a following 0, so the whole array is kept, sum 24; the original output dropped elements. Example 3: delete the interval from the first 1 to the following 0, keeping 0, 6, 2, sum 8; the original output omitted the 6.
hints: Find the last 0 in the array. While scanning, a 1 before it enters the deleting state and a 0 exits it; any 1 after the last 0 can never be closed, so everything there is kept.
